summary: Extends the Sieve notification extension to define presence information that can be checked through the notify_method_capability feature. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: Lets your mail filter ask whether you are online or busy before deciding what to do with a new message.

questions: how to check presence in a sieve script
what does the sieve show item mean
subtitle: Lets a Sieve mail filter check whether you are busy, away or offline before it decides how to notify you.

tldr.problem: Sieve notifications are sent regardless of what the user is doing, but it is often desirable to tailor them to the user's current situation.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers three presence items (busy, show and status) as notification-capability parameters, which a script tests with the notify_method_capability test from the Sieve Notify extension.
tldr.outcome: Scripts can skip notifications when the user is busy or answer senders using the user's status text. Implementations must protect presence data with access controls.

facts.label: show values
facts.value: away, chat, dnd, offline, xa, unknown

today: RFC 6132 is a Proposed Standard from July 2011. It is not obsoleted or updated by any RFC listed in its metadata.

sections.title: Why Presence Matters to Sieve
sections.content:
Sieve (RFC 5228) is a mail filtering language. Its Notification extension (RFC 5435) can send alerts when mail arrives, and already defines a way to test presence: the notify_method_capability test, with one test, the "online" notification-capability.

RFC 6132 adds more presence tests by registering extra notification-capability parameters in the IANA registry. The goal is to tailor notifications to a user's current situation.
sections.eli5: A mail filter can already send you a ping. This lets it first check whether you are in the mood to be pinged.

sections.title: Testing Presence Items
sections.content:
When mail arrives, a script running for the user passes the user's presence URI in the notification-uri parameter, names an item in notification-capability and compares it with values in key-list. Any item may also have the value unknown if it cannot be determined.

If a script tests the same item more than once in one execution, implementations MUST give the same value each time, for example by caching it on first use. There is no capability string for this extension, but it requires support for enotify. If the interpreter does not know the item, RFC 5435 already says the test fails without an error.

It is only a condition test, so any Sieve action can appear inside it. The RFC says it is not tied to XMPP (RFC 6121) or any particular presence source, and expects future extensions to add items such as calendar or location data.
sections.eli5: The filter asks one question about you, gets one answer, and sticks to that answer for the rest of the check, so it does not change its mind halfway.

sections.title: The Three Presence Items
sections.content:
busy says whether the user is considered busy now, with values yes, no or unknown. What busy means is left to the implementation and may be derived from other information, including show.

show is the formal availability status, similar to the element of the same name in RFC 6121. Its values are away, chat, dnd (do not disturb), offline, xa (extended away) and unknown.

status is a free-form, human-readable description in any language. Comparing it directly is unlikely to be useful, so it is meant to be pulled into a variable (RFC 5229) and reused, for example in an auto-reply. Because users may write it, no value, including unknown, has special meaning. An empty string may be best when it cannot be determined.
sections.eli5: There are three signs: a yes or no busy sign, a menu of moods like away or do not disturb, and a sticky note you write yourself.

sections.title: Example Scripts
sections.content:
The first example sends an XMPP notification only if the recipient is not busy, and sends nothing if the busy test is unsupported. The second flips the logic with not and "yes", so a notification is sent when busy is unsupported.

The third uses the vacation extension (RFC 5230) to auto-reply when the sender is in the recipient's address book (RFC 6134) and the recipient's show is xa. It uses the variables extension to put the status text into the reply, with a fallback message if none is available.
sections.eli5: One rule says only ping me when I am free. Another says if I am away, send a friend an automatic note with my own words.

sections.title: Privacy and Load Risks
sections.content:
Security considerations for Sieve and the Notify extension apply. Implementations MUST ensure users cannot write scripts that read other people's presence information without proper access controls.

A script can act on presence that the message sender is not allowed to see. A sender could then probe the recipient's presence if messages sometimes trigger auto-replies and sometimes do not.

Many messages arriving at once could overload a shared presence server. Implementations might add rate limiting or caching. Cached results MUST NOT be used outside the context in which they were retrieved: a result fetched for Adam's script about Barbara may be reused for Adam, but not for Cindy.
sections.eli5: Your busy sign should be seen only by people allowed to see it. Someone could also learn when you are away by noticing when you stop answering, so be careful with auto-replies.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The RFC registers busy, show and status as notification-capability parameters. For busy and show, the value MUST be lower case. Future presence items should be registered the same way, following Section 9.3 of RFC 5435. The contact for all three is the Sieve discussion list.
sections.eli5: The three signs are written in an official list so every mail system uses the same names.

items.label: Chat
items.desc: Online and actively interested in chatting.

items.label: Do not disturb
items.desc: The user does not wish to be disturbed now.

items.label: Unknown
items.desc: The correct value could not be determined.
